titleText.es: Nuestros cerebros solo tienen una escala y lo que hacemos es redimensionar nuestras experiencias para que encajen.
titleText.en: Our brains have just one scale, and we resize our experiences to fit.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish and official title attributes are preserved exactly. Vision split SOPORTAR, PROBADO, CUALQUIERA, FOTOGRAMAS, ABURRIDOS, and ALABANDO at genuine printed line wraps; each is one lexical occurrence. It also omitted several third-panel and lower-panel words and misread accents, letters, the Wikipedia name, and the abbreviated frame labels. WIKIPEDIA, JOE BIDEN, J.B., and the four numeric labels are audited exclusions.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: This sense of soportar is about tolerating something unpleasant, not physically supporting weight.

example.en: I cannot put up with that noise.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Barato describes a masculine singular thing with a low price.

example.en: We bought an inexpensive watch.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Vinos is the plural of vino.

example.es: La tienda vende vinos de varias regiones.
example.en: The shop sells wines from several regions.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to me; marks the person who experiences a taste
cardDefinitions.noteEn: With saber in its taste sense, me identifies the speaker as the person to whom something tastes a certain way.

example.en: The tea tastes sweet to me.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Saben is a plural present form of saber. With a taste description, saber means “to taste,” not “to know.”

example.en: These apples taste tart.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Igual can describe two or more experiences as the same.

example.en: The two versions sound the same.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Prestaras is the -ra form used for an imagined condition. In prestar atención, prestar means “to pay.”

example.en: If you paid attention, you would remember more.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Verías is ver with the conditional ending -ías.

example.es: Con más luz, verías el detalle.
example.en: With more light, you would see the detail.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Para can introduce the subject or case to which a statement applies.

example.es: La regla es válida para cualquier caso.
example.en: The rule is valid for any case.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: House is an internationally used name for a style of electronic dance music.

example.en: The club plays house music.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: In tipo de letra, letra refers to the visual design used for written characters.

example.es: Elige un tipo de letra sencillo.
example.en: Choose a simple typeface.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Firmas is the plural of firma.

example.en: The document needs two signatures.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Porno is a common shortened form of pornografía.

example.en: The platform blocks pornographic content.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Surrealista has the same form with masculine and feminine singular nouns.

example.en: We watched a surreal film.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: devote time to it or them (informal command)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Dedica is the affirmative tú command of dedicar, and attached le represents the target receiving the time or attention.

example.en: Devote an hour to the project.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Cualquiera can stand alone for any one person or thing in a stated group.

example.es: Puedes elegir cualquiera de estas rutas.
example.en: You can choose any one of these routes.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: you will become; you will turn into
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Convertirás is the future form used for one familiar listener; with te and en it expresses becoming.

example.es: Con práctica, te convertirás en experta.
example.en: With practice, you will become an expert.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Connoisseur is a borrowed noun for someone with refined knowledge and judgment in a field.

example.en: He is a coffee connoisseur.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Esnob can be a noun or an adjective for someone who displays supposedly superior taste.

example.en: His comment sounded snobbish.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Profundidad can be physical depth or the amount of complexity and richness in a subject.

example.en: The essay has a lot of depth.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Metes is the informal singular present form of meter.

example.es: Metes los libros en una caja.
example.en: You put the books in a box.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Comiendo is the ongoing-action form of comer, and se can emphasize consuming the item completely.

example.es: El niño está comiéndose una manzana.
example.en: The child is eating an apple.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: The written accent keeps the stress on the first syllable.

example.en: She made a cheese sandwich.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Estarán is the third-person plural future form of estar.

example.en: Tomorrow they will be ready.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Convencidos describes a masculine or mixed plural group that firmly believes something.

example.en: They are convinced that it will work.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: of; no separate English word before que after convencido
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Convencido requires de before a noun or before que plus the belief.

example.en: I am convinced that she will come.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Geniales has one form for masculine and feminine plural subjects.

example.en: Both ideas are brilliant.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Horribles has one form for masculine and feminine plural subjects.

example.en: Those noises are awful.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Exageras is the informal singular present form of exagerar.

example.en: I think you are exaggerating the problem.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: La mayoría de introduces the larger part of a group.

example.es: La mayoría de los alumnos llegó temprano.
example.en: Most of the students arrived early.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Boca names the mouth as a body part.

example.en: He closed his mouth.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Cerrada is the feminine singular completed-action form used as a description.

example.en: The door is closed.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Aburridos describes masculine plural things that cause boredom.

example.en: The speeches were boring.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Mandíbula is the lower or upper bony structure that holds the teeth.

example.en: Her jaw hurts.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Enmarca is the present form for one thing that surrounds or visually highlights another.

example.en: The window frames the landscape.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Mayonesa is the standard Spanish word for mayonnaise.

example.en: She added mayonnaise to the sandwich.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Before an abstract noun, puro or pura can intensify it with the sense “sheer” or “nothing but.”

example.en: The news was pure joy.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: what a; what (before a noun in an exclamation)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Qué keeps its accent when it introduces an exclamation such as ¡qué sorpresa!

example.en: What an idea!

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Novedad names something new or unexpected; it can also appear sarcastically in an exclamation.

example.es: Esa noticia no es ninguna novedad.
example.en: That news is nothing new.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Alabando is the ongoing-action form of alabar.

example.es: Siguió alabando el trabajo del equipo.
example.en: She kept praising the team's work.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: A fotograma is one still image in a film, animation, or video sequence.

example.en: They analyzed every frame of the video.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to listen to you; to hear you
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Escuchar stays in its dictionary form and te attaches to represent one familiar listener.

example.en: On listening to you, I understood the problem.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Diría is the conditional form of decir for I, he, she, or formal you.

example.en: I would say that it is enough.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Francamente is an adverb formed from franca plus -mente.

example.en: Frankly, I do not agree.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Dar can describe light striking or falling on a place.

example.es: La luz da en la pared.
example.en: The light falls on the wall.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Cuello names the body part between the head and torso.

example.es: Lleva una bufanda en el cuello.
example.en: She wears a scarf around her neck.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Lechuga is the leafy vegetable lettuce.

example.en: He put lettuce in the salad.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Colocaría is the conditional form of colocar for I, he, she, or formal you. In a list, it can mean “would rank.”

example.es: Yo la colocaría entre las mejores.
example.en: I would rank it among the best.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Top is a common loanword for the highest positions in a ranking.

example.es: La canción entró en el top diez.
example.en: The song entered the top ten.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How does saber express how food or drink tastes to someone?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Name the food or drink, use the matching small experiencer pronoun plus a form of saber, and add the taste description.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The thing tasted controls singular sabe or plural saben. The pronoun identifies who experiences the taste.

example.es: A Marta, las aceitunas le saben saladas.
example.en: To Marta, the olives taste salty.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How can Spanish emphasize the person who experiences a feeling, preference, or taste?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Add a plus the person for emphasis or clarification, while keeping the matching small pronoun before the verb.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The a phrase clarifies or contrasts the experiencer; it does not replace me, te, le, nos, os, or les.

example.es: A mí me gusta el té.
example.en: I like tea.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How can you describe a subject as a whole rich world of its own?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Todo adds an emphatic “whole” sense before un mundo.

example.es: La astronomía es todo un mundo.
example.en: Astronomy is a whole world of its own.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: What is the common Spanish expression for a typeface or font?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Tipo can change to plural tipos when more than one typeface is meant.

example.en: I prefer this typeface.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: dedicar tiempo a + persona, cosa o actividad
cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone devotes time to a person, thing, or activity?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use dedicar tiempo a, followed by the target.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The form of dedicar changes with the subject and time. A introduces what receives the time.

example.en: I devote time to learning languages.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you introduce something that a person is convinced is true?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use the matching form of estar convencido, then de que, then the belief.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Convencido changes to match the person or group described.

example.en: We are convinced that it will work.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you refer to most members of a group?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use la mayoría de, followed by the group.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The following noun phrase names the complete group from which the majority is taken.

example.es: La mayoría de los trenes llegó a tiempo.
example.en: Most of the trains arrived on time.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you exclaim about a person, thing, or situation named by a noun?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Put accented qué directly before the noun and use exclamation marks.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: No article is inserted between qué and the noun.

example.en: What a surprise!

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you present a concession based on an unreal or counterfactual situation?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use aunque followed by the special past-looking subjunctive form in -ra or -se.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: This pattern says the main result would hold even under the imagined condition.

example.en: I would go even if it rained.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: Why do the characters develop elaborate judgments about nearly identical images?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Sustained attention creates expertise and a finer internal scale, even when the subject initially seems shallow or arbitrary.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The joke begins with a claim that careful attention reveals a whole world in any subject. An artificial year-long exposure to near-identical sandwich images then produces confident aesthetic distinctions, parodying both genuine expertise and snobbery.

example.es: Con práctica, una persona distingue matices que antes parecían iguales.
example.en: With practice, a person distinguishes nuances that once seemed identical.

applications.explanationEn: Más raises the degree of profundidad, and que introduces the comparison.
Si introduces a condition presented as possible.
Metes is the ordinary present form used in the possible condition.
A marks the person-denoting object gente.
Se presents the eating as consumption of the specified item.
Al final marks the eventual outcome.
Estarán states the future result of the earlier si condition.
Estar keeps its whole dictionary form and adds -án for a plural future subject.
Estarán and plural convencidos describe the group, while de que introduces its belief.
Tú is stated to contrast or challenge the other speaker's judgment.
Question marks and intonation turn tú crees into a yes-or-no question without an extra helper.
